item.title: [机器人] 德州超级工厂钢构约55%：年产千万Optimus
item.author: @JoeTegtmeyer
item.description:
Joe Tegtmeyer称Giga Texas的Optimus工厂建设推进迅速，规划年产最高1000万台人形机器人、面积超700万平方英尺；主钢结构约55%已组装，目标2027年底极小规模投产。

@JoeTegtmeyer · 赞 225 · 转 21 · 浏览 7613

Want to know how the @Tesla Optimus factory under construction at Giga Texas is progressing? I’d say it is moving along at warp speed! This facility is to manufacture up to 10M/year humanoid robots & will be over 7 million sq ft (~3,500 ft long) once completed including a substantial part of the factory using 4 floors! This factory is in addition to the pilot line at Fremont that has reportedly already begun small-scale production. Right now, the main steel structure is ~55% assembled with a noticeable widening of the surrounding ground grading & reclamation of a large section of abandoned sand & gravel mining area on the E side of the new factory. As I understand it, the target is to have the entire steel structure assembled with final topping ceremony held around the end of March 2027. This won’t be the end of construction as it will still need a lot more to complete the facility, install the production equipment & have utilities connected, particularly power, so massive construction work will continue throughout most of 2027. The approach to construction of this factory differs significantly to the approach used for the main Giga Texas factory in that it will be substantially closed in before major equipment is installed. There are also some ground level utilities, footings and final perimeter grade beam work underway, with the E side of the building now taking shape with what appears to be a large open section about 4 column grids wide along this side of the facility. Per Tesla the goal will be to be able to begin some *very limited* production here sometime at the end of 2027 & then scale up production capability from there through 2028.

item.title: [机器人] RoboColosseum真实机器人评测上线
item.author: @TheHumanoidHub
item.description:
RoboColosseum在真实硬件上盲测机器人策略，覆盖150多场景并公开含失败在内的全部rollout；已测OpenAI、Anthropic、NVIDIA等30余策略，学术实验室可获1万小时免费评测。

@TheHumanoidHub · 赞 14 · 转 3 · 浏览 2288

Robotics finally has its real-world arena. RoboColosseum is a real-world benchmark that tests robot policies on hundreds of actual robots across 150+ scenes, not cherry-picked demos. You bring a model, they run it blind on real hardware and publish every rollout (failures included) on Hugging Face. Two ways models are tested: - Open track: two unnamed models get the same brand-new instruction in the same scene. A human judge watches both runs and picks the winner, or a tie. Think LMArena, but on real robots. It measures zero-shot performance on novel tasks. - Fine-tune track: every model is fine-tuned on one fixed task from the same open-source demos, then gets 25 attempts. An apples-to-apples test of how well a model learns a specific skill. Over 30 policies from OpenAI, Anthropic, NVIDIA, Galaxea, Ai2 and more are tested across Unitree G1, Franka, YAM and SO-101. Why it matters: across 20,000+ real runs, no model won everywhere. Rankings flipped depending on the task and the robot body. That's the whole point: a single demo or benchmark tells you almost nothing about what a policy can actually do. This is the field finally getting honest, real robots, in the wild, every failure published. And 10,000 eval hours are free for academic labs. https://t.co/bRNf0LcD9R
